definition_en: the one in position five, or one of five equal parts

definition_en: to get something after searching, to discover something, or to consider it a certain way
core_image: 孩子在书包里翻找，终于摸到丢失的钥匙
scene: 孩子在书包里翻找，终于摸到丢失的钥匙。I cannot find my keys.
sceneCN: 这里 find 是「找到」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我找不到我的钥匙。

senses.title: To get by searching
senses.example: I cannot find my keys.
senses.why: Old English findan meant to come upon something; the modern verb keeps the picture of reaching a thing you were looking for.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 findan 意为「遇到、碰到」；现代动词保留的是找到正在寻找之物的画面。

senses.title: To discover by chance
senses.definition: to discover something not looked for
senses.example: We found a small cat under the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在桥下发现一只小猫。
senses.why: Because coming upon a thing does not require a search, the same verb also covers discoveries made by chance.
senses.whyCN: 因为碰到一样东西并不一定需要寻找，同一个动词也涵盖偶然的发现。

senses.title: To consider
senses.definition: to consider something to be a certain way
senses.example: I find this book very interesting.
senses.why: English extended find from finding a thing to finding it to be so, and the verb now reports an opinion formed by experience.
senses.whyCN: 英语把 find 从「找到东西」扩展到「发现它是这样」，这个词于是表达由经历形成的看法。

definition_en: to complete something, to come to an end, or to use up the last of something
core_image: 跑道上选手冲过终点线，计时牌停下
scene: 跑道上选手冲过终点线，计时牌停下。She finished the race first.
sceneCN: 这里 finish 是「完成」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她第一个跑完比赛。

senses.title: To complete
senses.example: She finished the race first.
senses.why: Finish comes from Latin finis, 'end'; to finish is to bring a piece of work to its end.
senses.whyCN: finish 源自拉丁语 finis「终点」；to finish 就是把一件事做到终点。

senses.title: To come to an end
senses.example: The film finishes at nine.
senses.why: The same end-point idea works without an object: a thing that reaches its end is said to finish.

definition_en: to repair something, to hold it in place, or to settle a time
core_image: 修车铺里，师傅把松动的车把拧紧
scene: 修车铺里，师傅把松动的车把拧紧。He fixed my bike in ten minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 fix 是「修理」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他十分钟就修好了我的自行车。

senses.title: To repair
senses.example: He fixed my bike in ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他十分钟就修好了我的自行车。
senses.why: Fix comes from Latin figere, 'fasten'; repairing something often means fastening its parts again, and the word kept that practical picture.
senses.whyCN: fix 源自拉丁语 figere「固定」；修理往往就是把零件重新固定住，这个词保留了这一实在的画面。

senses.title: To fasten in place
senses.definition: to make something stay in place
senses.example: Fix the picture to the wall.
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply to fasten, and it survives whenever something is attached so that it cannot move.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是「固定」，凡是把东西装牢、使之不能移动的场合都保留了这个意思。

senses.title: To settle
senses.definition: to arrange or settle a time
senses.example: Let us fix a date for the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把旅行的日期定下来吧。
senses.why: Because a settled arrangement is something fastened down, the verb extended from physical fixing to fixing a date or price.
senses.whyCN: 因为定下来的安排就像钉牢一样，这个动词从实物固定扩展到确定日期或价格。

senses.definition: the bottom of the sea or a valley
senses.example: The diver reached the ocean floor.
senses.why: The 'bottom surface' sense extends to nature, naming the ground under water or at the base of a valley.
senses.whyCN: 「底部表面」的意思扩展到自然，指水下或谷底的那层地面。

definition_en: to move through the air, to travel by plane, or to wave in the wind
core_image: 操场上风筝线拉直，风筝在风里越飞越高
scene: 操场上风筝线拉直，风筝在风里越飞越高。The kite flies high in the wind.
sceneCN: 这里 fly 是「飞」（第 01 个义项）；句意是风筝在风中飞得很高。

senses.title: To move through the air
senses.example: The kite flies high in the wind.
senses.why: Old English fleogan meant to move through the air on wings; the modern verb keeps that plain picture.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 fleogan 意为「用翅膀在空中移动」；现代动词保留的就是这幅简单的画面。

senses.title: To travel by plane
senses.example: We fly to Beijing every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 我们每年春天乘飞机去北京。
senses.why: Because an aircraft is the machine that flies, the verb came to mean travelling by one, with the passenger as subject.
senses.whyCN: 因为飞机就是会飞行的机器，这个词就表示乘它出行，主语是乘客。

senses.title: To wave in the wind
senses.definition: to wave or float in the air
senses.example: The flag flies above the gate.
senses.why: A light object held by the wind also 'flies', so flags and hair are said to fly in a breeze.
senses.whyCN: 被风托住的轻物也算「飞」，所以旗子和头发在风中被说成 fly。

definition_en: what people or animals eat, a kind of dish, or material that feeds plants
core_image: 餐桌上摆着一碗热汤、一盘米饭和一碟青菜

sceneCN: 这里 food 是「食物」（第 01 个义项）；句意是食物够所有人吃。

senses.title: What people eat
senses.example: There is enough food for everyone.
senses.why: Old English foda meant nourishment; the word names whatever is eaten to keep a body alive.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 foda 意为「养料」；这个词指为维持生命而吃下的一切。

senses.title: A cuisine or dish
senses.definition: a particular kind or dish of food
senses.example: I love Chinese food.
senses.why: The same mass noun is used for a cuisine or a dish, naming food by its style rather than by its substance.
senses.whyCN: 同一个不可数名词也用来指某种菜系或菜式，按风格而不是按物质来指食物。

senses.title: Material that feeds plants
senses.example: Plant food helps the roses grow.
senses.exampleCN: 花肥能让玫瑰长得更好。
senses.why: Because the word means nourishment in general, it also names what is fed to plants, as in plant food.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词泛指养分，它也指喂给植物的东西，如 plant food。

definition_en: to trick someone, to make them look silly, or to behave in a silly way
core_image: 愚人节里，同学指着同桌的鞋带说散了，其实没散
scene: 愚人节里，同学指着同桌的鞋带说散了，其实没散。Do not fool your friends with that trick.
sceneCN: 这里 fool 是「欺骗」（第 01 个义项）；句意是别用那个把戏骗朋友。

senses.title: To trick
senses.definition: to trick someone into believing something
senses.example: Do not fool your friends with that trick.
senses.why: Fool comes from Latin follis, 'bellows, windbag'; a person who talks empty words was called a fool, and the verb came to mean tricking someone.
senses.whyCN: fool 源自拉丁语 follis「风箱、空袋子」；说空话的人被叫作傻瓜，动词便由此表示骗人。

senses.title: To make look silly
senses.example: The joke fooled everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这个玩笑愚弄了屋里所有人。
senses.why: The verb widened from plain deception to making a person appear foolish, which is what a practical joke does.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从单纯的欺骗扩展到让人显得愚蠢，恶作剧做的正是这件事。

senses.title: To behave silly
senses.definition: to behave in a silly way
senses.example: Stop fooling around and do your homework.
senses.why: The phrase fool around turns the word toward the subject's own silly behaviour instead of a trick played on someone.
senses.whyCN: fool around 这个说法把词义转向主语自己胡闹，而不是对别人设套。

items.en: Follis meant bellows or a windbag.
items.cn: 拉丁语 follis 指风箱或空袋子。

items.en: A person of empty talk was called a fool.
items.cn: 说空话的人被叫作傻瓜。

items.en: The verb came to mean to trick.

items.en: It widened to making someone look silly.

items.en: Fool covers tricks and silly behaviour.
items.cn: 现代英语中它涵盖骗局与胡闹。

examples.en: Do not fool your friends with that trick.
The joke fooled everyone in the room.

examples.en: Stop fooling around and do your homework.

root: 源自拉丁语 follis「风箱、空袋子」，说空话的人被称为 fool，动词由此表示欺骗，后扩展到愚弄与胡闹。

sensesIntro.en: Fool means to trick someone, to make them look silly, or to behave in a silly way.
sensesIntro.cn: fool 指欺骗某人、使人显得可笑，也指自己胡闹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: on April Fool's Day a classmate points at a friend's shoelace and says it is undone when it is not
core.cn: 核心意象：愚人节里，同学指着同桌的鞋带说散了，其实没散

branches.en: JOKE: a trick played for fun.
SELF: silly behaviour without a target.
branches.cn: 自身线：没有对象的胡闹。
